# remoteclient

```go
import remoteclient "pocketone.dev/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient"
```

Package remoteclient is remote/v1's CLI client: the remotes a project links (.pocketone/remotes.yaml), saved logins, sign-in (an API token, a password, or OAuth in the browser or with a device code), and an authenticated HTTP client for a remote. ext/remotes' commands and other extensions' commands (deploy) build on it.

Package remotes gives the command named remotes: other PocketBase instances (or PocketHost instances) a project deploys to, signed in once with \`pocketone login\`.

	pocketone remote add prod https://myapp.example.com
	pocketone login prod
	pocketone deploy prod

Remote names and URLs live in the project's .pocketbase/remotes.json (commit it); secrets live in the user's ~/.config/pocketone/credentials.json (0600), keyed by URL. P1\_TOKEN overrides the saved login (CI sets it). The folder is named after [extkit.Command](/pocketone.dev/ext/extkit#Command) (~/.config/pockethost in that build); the variables are PocketOne's (P1\_) in every build.

The server half is remote/v1's whoami (GET /api/\_c/remote/v1): who the request's token is, its scopes, and which contracts the app offers (deploy/v1, oauth/v1, api-tokens/v1, ...), so clients discover what a remote supports.

Source: [`ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient`](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient).

## Constants

<a id="projectdir"></a><a id="projectfile"></a><a id="defaultname"></a>

```go
const (
	// ProjectDir holds the project's remotes file. Not a pb_* name: pb_* folders are deployed.
	ProjectDir  = ".pocketbase"
	ProjectFile = "remotes.json"

	// DefaultName is the remote used when a command names none and the project sets no default.
	DefaultName = "default"
)
```

<a id="accountsuperusers"></a>

```go
const AccountSuperusers = "_superusers"
```

AccountSuperusers is the account the CLI signs in as by default: an app's superusers.

<a id="oauthclientid"></a>

```go
const OAuthClientId = "pocketone-cli"
```

OAuthClientId is the built-in public client of the OAuth server in ext/api-tokens.

<a id="passwordtokenttl"></a>

```go
const PasswordTokenTTL = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
```

PasswordTokenTTL is how long a password login lasts: the session is swapped for a token of this length (PocketBase's impersonate, which a superuser may do for itself), so it lasts like a browser login. Changing the superuser's password ends it.

<a id="whoamipath"></a>

```go
const WhoamiPath = "/api/_c/remote/v1"
```

WhoamiPath is remote/v1's whoami (public): who the caller is and what the remote offers.

## Variables

<a id="canopenbrowser"></a>

```go
var CanOpenBrowser = canOpenBrowser
```

CanOpenBrowser reports whether a browser can be opened here: false over SSH or on a Linux box without a display, so the login uses a device code instead (overridable for tests, with [OpenBrowser](#openbrowser)).

<a id="errnowhoami"></a>

```go
var ErrNoWhoami = errors.New("the remote doesn't offer remote/v1")
```

ErrNoWhoami: the remote doesn't offer remote/v1 (no remotes extension, e.g. a PocketHost edge today).

<a id="errnotloggedin"></a>

```go
var ErrNotLoggedIn = errors.New("not logged in")
```

ErrNotLoggedIn is returned by [Open](#open) when there's no credential for the remote.

<a id="openbrowser"></a>

```go
var OpenBrowser = func(u string) error {
	switch runtime.GOOS {
	case "darwin":
		return exec.Command("open", u).Start()
	case "windows":
		return exec.Command("rundll32", "url.dll,FileProtocolHandler", u).Start()
	default:
		return exec.Command("xdg-open", u).Start()
	}
}
```

OpenBrowser opens url in the user's browser (overridable for tests).

<a id="retrysleep"></a>

```go
var RetrySleep = func(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) error {
	t := time.NewTimer(d)
	defer t.Stop()
	select {
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	case <-t.C:
		return nil
	}
}
```

RetrySleep waits d before a rate-limited request is sent again, or until ctx ends (overridable for tests).

<a id="useragent"></a>

```go
var UserAgent = "pocketone-cli"
```

UserAgent is sent with every client request.

## Functions

### ConfigDir

```go
func ConfigDir() (string, error)
```

ConfigDir is the user's config folder, named after [extkit.Command](/pocketone.dev/ext/extkit#Command): $P1\_CONFIG\_DIR, else $XDG\_CONFIG\_HOME/pocketone, else ~/.config/pocketone.

### DecodeResponse

```go
func DecodeResponse(res *http.Response, out any) error
```

DecodeResponse turns a non-2xx response into an [APIError](#apierror) (PocketBase's {message} or the deploy API's), else decodes JSON into out.

### EnvToken

```go
func EnvToken() (token, source string)
```

EnvToken returns the token in P1\_TOKEN, which overrides the saved login for whatever remote a command uses, and the variable's name as its source. Set it for one command (\`P1\_TOKEN=... pocketone deploy staging\`) to use another token for that command only.

### EnvVar

```go
func EnvVar(suffix string) string
```

EnvVar is PocketOne's environment variable for suffix ([extkit.EnvVar](/pocketone.dev/ext/extkit#EnvVar)): EnvVar("TOKEN") is P1\_TOKEN. in pocketone.

### FindProjectRoot

```go
func FindProjectRoot(dir string) string
```

FindProjectRoot walks up from dir to the nearest folder with .pocketbase/remotes.json. None: dir itself.

### IsStatus

```go
func IsStatus(err error, status int) bool
```

IsStatus reports whether err is an [APIError](#apierror) with this status.

### NewHTTPClient

```go
func NewHTTPClient() *http.Client
```

NewHTTPClient returns the HTTP client remote commands use: short connect and TLS timeouts, no overall timeout (uploads and log streams run long; callers pass contexts).

### NormalizeURL

```go
func NormalizeURL(raw string) (string, error)
```

NormalizeURL checks an instance URL and trims it to scheme://host\[:port]\[/path] without a trailing slash. A bare host gets https://.

### RevokeOAuth

```go
func RevokeOAuth(ctx context.Context, c *Client, cr *Credential) error
```

RevokeOAuth revokes an OAuth login's refresh token (and with it the access token) on the remote.

SaveLogin stores a login for the client's remote URL.

ValidName reports whether s can name a remote.

### Open

```go
func Open(dir, name string) (*Client, error)
```

Open resolves a remote of the project containing dir (name may be empty or a URL, see [Project.Resolve](#projectresolve)) and its credential: the CI environment first ([EnvToken](#envtoken)), then the saved login. With no credential it returns the client and an error wrapping [ErrNotLoggedIn](#errnotloggedin).

### Credential

```go
type Credential struct {
	Token string `json:"token"`
	// Via: "token" (a pasted pbt_ or PocketHost token), "jwt" (a pasted PocketBase auth token), "oauth".
	Via          string    `json:"via"`
	Email        string    `json:"email,omitempty"`
	Collection   string    `json:"collection,omitempty"`
	RefreshToken string    `json:"refreshToken,omitempty"`
	Expires      time.Time `json:"expires,omitzero"`
	// TokenEndpoint and RevokeEndpoint (OAuth logins) refresh and revoke it.
	TokenEndpoint  string    `json:"tokenEndpoint,omitempty"`
	RevokeEndpoint string    `json:"revokeEndpoint,omitempty"`
	Created        time.Time `json:"created"`
}
```

Credential is a saved sign-in for one URL.

### LoginOptions

```go
type LoginOptions struct {
	// Token, if set, is used as is (pbt_..., a PocketHost token, or a JWT).
	Token string
	// TokenFrom, if set, gives the token on its first line (--token-stdin).
	TokenFrom io.Reader
	// Browser is the OAuth sign-in tried first on a remote that offers oauth/v1 (normally [OAuthLogin]); nil skips it.
	// It may return (nil, nil) to fall back to the token prompt.
	Browser   func(ctx context.Context, c *Client, w *Whoami, opts BrowserLoginOptions) (*LoginResult, error)
	Device    bool // device code instead of a browser redirect
	NoBrowser bool // print the sign-in URL instead of opening a browser
	// Prompt is where the sign-in is asked for when nothing else signed in (a superuser's email, or a pasted token);
	// nil means there's no terminal to ask in.
	Prompt io.Reader
	// Password reads a password without echoing it (nil: read a line from Prompt).
	Password func(prompt string) (string, error)
	// Out gets the prompts and the result line.
	Out io.Writer
}
```

LoginOptions configure [Login](#login).

### LoginResult

```go
type LoginResult struct {
	Credential *Credential
	// Warning, if set, is shown to the user.
	Warning string
	// TokenId is the API token's id, when the remote reports one.
	TokenId string
}
```

LoginResult is a finished sign-in, ready to save.

### Login

```go
func Login(ctx context.Context, c *Client, opts LoginOptions) (*LoginResult, error)
```

Login signs in to the client's remote, saves the login and says who it signed in as: with opts.Token or opts.TokenFrom when given, else in the browser when the remote offers OAuth, else at opts.Prompt with a superuser's email and password ([PasswordLogin](#passwordlogin)) or a pasted token. It's the sign-in behind \`login\`, \`link\` and \`clone\`.

### LoginWithToken

```go
func LoginWithToken(ctx context.Context, c *Client, token string) (*LoginResult, error)
```

LoginWithToken checks a pasted token (pbt\_..., a PocketHost token, or a JWT) with the remote's whoami when it has one; a remote without whoami (a PocketHost edge today) takes it as is.

### OAuthLogin

```go
func OAuthLogin(ctx context.Context, c *Client, w *Whoami, opts BrowserLoginOptions) (*LoginResult, error)
```

OAuthLogin signs in through the remote's OAuth server: the browser with a loopback redirect and PKCE, or a device code (opts.Device, or when no browser can be opened here).

### PasswordLogin

```go
func PasswordLogin(ctx context.Context, c *Client, email, password string) (*LoginResult, error)
```

PasswordLogin signs in as one of the remote's superusers with email and password, through PocketBase's own auth API. It's for a remote with no browser sign-in (stock PocketBase, such as an instance a multisite host runs in Docker): the host checks the superuser's token with the instance. The session token is swapped for one of [PasswordTokenTTL](#passwordtokenttl) when the remote allows it.

### Whoami

```go
type Whoami struct {
	Auth *struct {
		Collection string `json:"collection"`
		Id         string `json:"id"`
		Email      string `json:"email"`
	} `json:"auth"`
	// Via: "token" (API token), "jwt", or "" (anonymous).
	Via     string   `json:"via"`
	Scopes  []string `json:"scopes"`
	TokenId string   `json:"tokenId"`
	// Contracts are the wire contracts the remote offers ("remote/v1", "deploy/v1"), each at /api/_c/<id>/.
	Contracts []string `json:"contracts"`
	App       struct {
		Name string `json:"name"`
		URL  string `json:"url"`
	} `json:"app"`
}
```

Whoami is remote/v1's whoami (GET /api/\_c/remote/v1).

### Whoami.Offers

```go
func (w *Whoami) Offers(id string) bool
```

Offers reports whether the remote offers a contract ("deploy/v1"): its API is at /api/\_c/\<id>/.
